cleared.check: Task 3 (L-960, L-976): Arbitrum retryable redeems at Nitro consensus-v61 and its go-ethereum fork. Is the callvalue of a scheduled redeem taken from the ticket escrow in state, and is transient storage empty when the redeem starts?
cleared.result: Yes to both. ArbitrumRetryTx in StartTxHook moves tx.Value from the escrow address to tx.From with util.TransferBalance, which fails with ErrInsufficientBalance when the escrow holds less (arbos/tx_processor.go lines 472-477; arbos/util/transfer.go lines 67-76), and tx.Value is the retryable callvalue stored at submission (arbos/retryables/retryable.go lines 366-381). At submission the callvalue is moved from the sender to the escrow with the same checked transfer (tx_processor.go line 320). The EVM call then checks CanTransfer for tx.From and debits it (fork core/state_transition.go line 725, core/vm/evm.go Call, core/evm.go lines 139-147). Each redeem, scheduled or made by ArbRetryableTx.redeem, runs as its own ApplyTransaction in the block loop (arbos/block_processor.go lines 373-375, 483, 612), and every transaction goes through StateDB.Prepare, which replaces transient storage before execution (fork core/state_transition.go line 737, core/state/statedb.go lines 1598-1599). A plain ArbitrumDepositTx mints and moves value without running any code (tx_processor.go lines 225-233), so it can only raise the PoolManager balance, which native settle does not read (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354). The fork was read at f3a966e, the pin of v3.11.3; the pin of consensus-v61 could not be confirmed without the GitHub API, and the same lines are identical on the fork master branch.

cleared.check: Task 3 (L-960): OP Stack deposits with a mint field. Is the CALLVALUE of a deposit debited from the sender after the mint?
cleared.result: Yes. op-geth adds the mint to msg.From before execution (core/state_transition.go lines 474-480) and then applies the ordinary CanTransfer check and EVM transfer of msg.value from msg.From (lines 574-579). op-revm at op-reth/v2.10.0-rc.4 adds the mint to the caller balance and subtracts the balance spending, and only raises the balance to the value when the configuration disables the balance check (rust/op-revm/src/handler.rs lines 137-151), a switch used by eth_call, not by block execution. The minted ETH was locked in the portal on L1 by the depositor, so the PoolManager is credited with value that its caller paid. The handler builds of Base, Zora, World Chain, Celo, X Layer and MegaETH were not read here; the op-stack-eth unit of this cycle covers failed deposits.

cleared.result: No. Tempo v1.19.1 (the endpoint answers tempo/v1.19.1-a9d6748) rejects any AA transaction in which a call carries a nonzero value, in intrinsic gas and in validation (crates/evm/src/handler.rs lines 372-375 and 1445-1448). Accounts hold no native balance, BALANCE returns 0 for the PoolManager (cycle 21), and eth_getBalance returns the placeholder 4242...42 for every address (queried for the PoolManager on rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz). Native settle on Tempo can only ever credit 0.

cleared.check: Task 3 (L-960): HyperEVM system transactions that carry HYPE value. Is the value debited?
cleared.result: In the public replica code, yes. hyper-evm-sync runs each system transaction through stock revm transact with the sender set to 0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222 for native HYPE, value from the transaction, base fee 0 and only EIP-3607 disabled; the balance check is not disabled, and a failed transact panics (src/run.rs lines 123-162 and 217-236). 0x2222...2222 holds 0x30d464db24353838a0d1e7d wei (about 944 million HYPE) on both the official endpoint and the archive client. Each system transaction is its own transact with a fresh journal, so transient storage starts empty. The closed validator itself was not read; its receipts are checked against this execution by the archive clients (run.rs line 236). No HyperEVM PoolManager native movement in the whole history escapes the traced frames (task 2).

cleared.check: Code reading: which functions reach _accountDelta and whether each is gated by the transient unlock flag.
cleared.result: _accountDelta (src/PoolManager.sol:368-379) is called only from take, settle and settleFor through _settle, clear, mint, burn and _accountPoolBalanceDelta, which is called only from modifyLiquidity, swap and donate (lines 181-183, 224-226, 270, 294, 317, 326, 334, 364). All nine carry onlyWhenUnlocked (lines 96-99, 147, 189, 258, 291, 300, 305, 310, 322, 332). The flag is set at line 107 and cleared at line 113 only after the delta count check at line 112. sync (lines 279-288), initialize, updateDynamicLPFee, the ERC-6909 functions and collectProtocolFees (src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57, controller only) need no unlock and write no currency delta. So every payout path depends on the transient flag and the count, as the theme assumes, and on these six networks no mined frame shows either failing.

leads.question: Can the PoolManager frames of mined Arc and Elysium transactions be checked by a source other than public RPC, for example an explorer internal transaction list that includes zero-value and failed frames, or a self-run Elysium Nitro node replaying from the parent chain?
leads.why: No public endpoint of either network serves traces, so the absence of a take outside unlock rests on the weaker log form, and Elysium native HYPE outflows (about 13,404 HYPE held) are not visible in logs at all.

leads.question: Repeat the unlock stack scan and the native balance reconciliation over evenly spaced windows of the whole history on MegaETH, Monad and Avalanche.
leads.why: This cycle covered only the most recent 1.6 million MegaETH blocks, 4,600 Monad blocks and 29,568 Avalanche blocks; Avalanche eth_getLogs was cut short by rate limits.

leadResults.answer: No such transaction on the four networks with public traces. HyperEVM whole history (2,838 transactions with a PoolManager frame), MegaETH blocks 31,271,626-32,856,625 (21,064), Monad blocks 125,430,073-125,434,672 (5,277), Avalanche blocks 101,367,460-101,397,027 (1,626): (a) 0, (b) 0, receipt and log agreement in every transaction, and the PoolManager native balance change equals the traced native flows to the wei on all four. Arc and Elysium serve no traces on any public endpoint; the weaker log form found no direct PoolManager call with a payout and no Transfer out without a matching inflow. The traces are re-executions by RPC nodes, not the producers, and the windows on MegaETH, Monad and Avalanche are recent ones.

On every system path read the CALLVALUE that reaches a contract is debited from a balance in state: Arbitrum retryable redeems (escrow to sender, then the EVM transfer), OP Stack deposits (mint to sender, then the EVM transfer), HyperEVM system transactions (stock revm from 0x2222...2222, in the public replica). Tempo batched calls cannot carry value at all. Native settle (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354) therefore credits only value its caller paid on these paths. The closed HyperEVM validator and the OP Stack builds with their own handler code were not read.

Yes to both at Nitro consensus-v61: the redeem callvalue moves from the ticket escrow with a checked transfer (arbos/tx_processor.go lines 472-477), and each redeem is a separate ApplyTransaction whose StateDB.Prepare resets transient storage (fork statedb.go lines 1598-1599, read at f3a966e; the exact pin of consensus-v61 is unconfirmed).
